text:
maya: quick heads-up — after the terraform change to svc/web-prod we saw the ALB target group mark targets unhealthy, app 503s for a few minutes. Any ideas?
kevin: do you mean k8s Service of type LoadBalancer or an Ingress? which change PR?
maya: PR #4123 — switched service to `nodePort` -> `LoadBalancer` with annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: external` and added `targetPort: 8080`, `port: 80`. The pods listen on 8080.
selena: can you paste the service yaml? sometimes port vs targetPort mismatch on the health check config with ALB/NLB.
maya: pasted below:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-prod
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "external"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: web
```
kevin: that looks fine on the K8s side. ALB health checks default to the instance port sometimes if target type is instance. Are we using `target-type: ip`?
maya: we did not set `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type`. default ended up being `instance` for this cluster.
selena: aha — with `instance` the NLB/ALB health check uses node port and node's hostPort mapping which can be 30000+; if the ASG security group doesn't allow that port healthcheck fails.
jonathan: quick check: what's the target group port showing in AWS console? If it's 8080 or 80?
maya: console shows target group port 80 and targets are the node IPs, port 30080. health check path is `/healthz` on port 80 apparently.
kevin: that's the mismatch. Two ways to fix: 1) set annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: ip` so ALB registers pod IPs on targetPort 8080 OR 2) set `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` + configure node security groups + nodePort healthcheck open.
selena: for our topology we prefer target-type ip for lower surface and correct LB routing. If you make that change ensure `podSecurityGroup` rules allow ELB health probes, and LB SG attaches to nodes/pods accordingly.
maya: updating PR to add `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: ip` and `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: HTTP` + `...-healthcheck-path: /healthz`. pinging for review.
kevin: also add `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: http` to be explicit.
jonathan: FYI if it's ALB with TLS termination at LB, make sure annotation `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-port` matches — we had one service where healthcheck used port 443 and backend was 8080 -> failed.
selena: good call. For PR review, check terraform/applied annotations not overridden by helm chart values.
maya: noted. @kevin @selena can you quick +1 the annotation change? I can roll it today after CI.
kevin: quick review done, looks fine. :thumbsup:
selena: LGTM. Also add a short runbook note in ops-runbooks about target-type differences.
infra-bot: deploy triggered for web-prod/service annotations update (deploy id: dpl-9087)
maya: thanks, will monitor healthchecks after the deploy and post timeseries if anything spikes.
jonathan: if it flaps again, we can fallback to rolling restart of pods to force target registration.
maya: copy — will update thread with results. :white_check_mark:
